paper: Can Foundation Models Wrangle Your Data? (Narayan, Chami, Orr, Arora, Ré)
task: Entity matching, error detection, schema matching, transformation, imputation
method: Prompting GPT-3 175B (text-davinci-002), zero- and few-shot
datasets_used: Magellan EM benchmark (Fodors-Zagats, Beer, iTunes-Amazon, Walmart-Amazon, DBLP-ACM, DBLP-Google, Amazon-Google); Synthea (schema matching); StackOverflow and Bing-QueryLogs (transformation); Restaurant and Buy (imputation); Hospital and Adult (error detection)
languages_covered: English in practice: authors note FMs are trained to model English; no non-English data evaluated
metrics: F1 for matching, error detection, schema matching; accuracy for imputation and transformation
weakness_or_gap: Brittle to prompt wording (about 9.4 F1 average gap); needs hand-picked demonstrations (about 14.7 F1 over random); weak on jargon-heavy data (Amazon-Google); privacy with API-only models; model bias can alter names (for example adding Ms.)
notes: Doc ref [1]. Read in full. Few-shot Hospital F1 97.8. Code: HazyResearch/fm_data_tasks

paper: Raha: A Configuration-Free Error Detection System (Mahdavi, Abedjan, Castro Fernandez, Madden, Ouzzani, Stonebraker, Tang)
method: Thousands of base detectors (outlier, pattern, rule/FD, knowledge-base), cell feature vectors, clustering, label propagation, about 20 labeled tuples
datasets_used: Flights and Beers named in the CIDR overview [4]; full list is in the Raha paper (not read)
languages_covered: Not stated; no non-English evaluation known (Raha paper not read)
weakness_or_gap: Signals are histogram and Gaussian outliers, character patterns, functional dependencies, and DBpedia checks; effect of one entity split across scripts is untested
notes: Doc ref [2]. Abstract and CIDR overview read; full paper not read. Baseline

paper: Structure-Guided Entity Resolution: Fine-Tuning LLMs for Robust Name Matching in Complex Linguistic Contexts (Chourasia, Kapoor, Patil)
method: Llama 3 8B, two-phase LoRA fine-tuning: parse name to first/middle/last JSON, then binary match; augmentation by pair swap, component permutation, space removal
datasets_used: Proprietary Dream11 KYC records: 20,000 curated labeled pairs expanded to over 50,000 by augmentation; disjoint test set of 50,000 real pairs; about 10,000 annotated names for phase 1
languages_covered: Indian names; Devanagari, Bengali, Tamil transliteration discussed; examples are Latin-script; Hindi and Hinglish not reported separately
metrics: Accuracy 99.02%, precision 99.95%, recall 98.9%, F1 0.994. Baseline F1: Levenshtein 0.726, multilingual BERT 0.806, GPT-4o few-shot 0.911, Llama 3 8B few-shot 0.839, SFT 0.946, SFT plus augmentation 0.973
weakness_or_gap: Name pairs only (no other fields); proprietary data, not reproducible; no cleaning or imputation; no verification of outputs; single organization; compound errors (whitespace, order, OCR) remain hard
notes: Doc ref [23]. Read in full. Closest work to TrustClean; reuse its baseline set for comparability
